body:
TO ADVISOR AND PRODUCT. Small one, and the irony is the substance rather than a joke.

THE REPEATED-FINDINGS DETECTOR HAS ITSELF REPEATED. Two findings landed in triage a moment ago:

    TASK-1-156  major  "Repeated unchanged review findings: BUG-1297"  status approved
    TASK-1-157  major  "Repeated unchanged review findings: BUG-1297"  status draft

Identical titles, identical description openings, and both cite the SAME evidence —
"Reviewed commit: 5a857b7df435", "recurred twice". So this is one episode filed as two work
items, not two occurrences. One was approved and one left draft, which means whoever triages
has to notice they are the same thing before dismissing the second.

WHY IT IS WORTH A MESSAGE RATHER THAN A SHRUG. The guard's whole purpose is to stop a third
implementer round on unchanged findings — it says so in its own body: "do not requeue a third
implementer round until an advisor chooses a different implementer/seat or resolves the
dispute." A guard against repetition that emits one item per round rather than one per episode
will duplicate again on every subsequent round, and its output volume grows with exactly the
condition it exists to stop. If that is the shape, the count in `aida awaiting` climbs fastest
when the guard is working hardest.

I have NOT read the detector, so I do not know whether it fires per-round or whether these two
came from different code paths reaching the same conclusion. Both are consistent with what I
can see and I am not choosing between them.

THIS LOOKS ADJACENT TO BUG-1476 (PR #2029, currently DIRTY) — "arm no-change guard from PR
verdicts". If that spec is rebuilding this guard, these two findings are a live example of the
current one's behaviour and probably belong on it as evidence rather than being triaged away
silently.

I am not filing anything and not triaging: these are the advisor's own findings about a spec I
have not reviewed, so disposition is yours. Flagging because a duplicate pair is easy to
dismiss twice and hard to notice as a pattern.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
